inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The argument property name.

inputFields.name: utilCall
inputFields.description: A nested function call.

inputFields.name: valueDict
inputFields.description: Defines a list of key-value pairs if this argument should be a dictionary.

inputFields.name: valueList
inputFields.description: Defines a list of values if this argument should be an array.

inputFields.name: valueLiteral

inputFields.name: valuePath

types.name: ActionBlokInput
types.description: An action's own blok (blok language v2): how a client shows a run of it in one context, naming devices by the action's dependency keys.

inputFields.name: catalog
inputFields.description: The catalog the blok is written for: the address it is published at (`https://arkitekt.live/catalogs/orkestrator/v1`), or the name of one registered in the organization. The base catalog, which every renderer draws, when absent. It is what `module` named before: one of the two is sent, and `module` is kept for an agent on an older spec.

inputFields.name: catalogMinor
inputFields.description: The minor of its catalog the blok needs: the newest `since` among the components and props it uses.

inputFields.name: catalogs
inputFields.description: The catalogs it needs, as name@version.

inputFields.name: components
inputFields.description: The UI component tree, unless the blok is sent as its `source`.

inputFields.name: context
inputFields.description: Where a client shows the run with it, as its `<Blok context=...>` says: PANEL in a task panel, SCENE as a 3D view (a `Scene`, or a `Space` placing the run's dependencies in a room whose layout is shared).

inputFields.name: demo
inputFields.description: What a preview renders it with.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: What the blok shows of a run.

inputFields.name: module
inputFields.description: The module the blok renders against besides its catalogs; the Orkestrator's when absent.

inputFields.name: phase
inputFields.description: When a client shows it, as its `<Blok kind=...>` says: RUN for a run of the action (kind action), ASSIGN before one, to start it (kind assign). One blok per context and phase.

inputFields.name: source
inputFields.description: The blok as v2 BSX, parsed by the server into its component tree. Exactly one of `components` and `source` is sent.

inputFields.name: vocab
inputFields.description: The blok language version the blok speaks; 2 is the only one.

types.name: ActionBlokPhase
types.description: When a client shows an action's own blok: RUN for a run of the action (it reads the run as `task`), ASSIGN before one, to start it (no `task`; `<args />` places the argument form, `assign.start()` starts the run).

types.name: ActionDemandInput
types.description:
Pure matching criteria for an action: hash or name short-circuits, arg/return
    port matches, protocols and forced port counts. Used directly by query filters and, wrapped
    in an ActionDependencyInput, by dependency declarations.

inputFields.name: app
inputFields.description: The identifier of the app providing the action, e.g. 'imagej'. Omit (or drop when loosening) to allow equivalent actions from any app.

inputFields.name: argMatches
inputFields.description: The matches the action's arg ports must satisfy.

inputFields.name: forceArgLength
inputFields.description: Require that the action has exactly this number of root args.

inputFields.name: forceReturnLength
inputFields.description: Require that the action has exactly this number of root returns.

inputFields.name: hash
inputFields.description: The exact hash of the action. When set, matching short-circuits on the hash and everything else is ignored.

inputFields.name: idempotent
inputFields.description: Require the action to be (or not be) idempotent. Omit to match either.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The action's key within its app, e.g. 'open_image'. Together with `app` this is the preferred identification of the demanded action.

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: The display name of the action to match.

inputFields.name: protocols
inputFields.description: Protocols (by name) the action must implement, e.g. 'predicate'.

inputFields.name: pure
inputFields.description: Require the action to be (or not be) pure. Omit to match either.

inputFields.name: returnMatches
inputFields.description: The matches the action's return ports must satisfy.

inputFields.name: stateful
inputFields.description: Require the action to be (or not be) stateful. Omit to match either.

inputFields.name: version
inputFields.description: The exact version of the action.

inputFields.name: optional

types.name: ActionKind

types.name: AgentCall

types.name: AgentDependencyInput
types.description:
A dependency for a implementation. By defining dependencies, you can
    create a dependency graph for your implementations and actions

inputFields.name: actionDependencies
inputFields.description: The named action requirements of the agent — each a slot key plus the demand the resolved action must satisfy.

inputFields.name: app
inputFields.description: Which app this dependency corresponds to (i.e. do you want to use a stardist agent for that or imagej agents needs to be a world unique classsifier (reverse domain notation) that identifies the type of agent you want to use, and then we can have multiple agents of the same type running in the system, e.g. startdist could be the app for all agents that correpsond to a startdist instance)

inputFields.name: autoResolvable
inputFields.description: Whether this dependency is auto resolvable or not. If so we will try to automatically resolve it based on the demands specified in the dependency and the capabilities of the available agents in the system. This is used to identify the demand in the system. Attention if any of the dependencies of this agent dependency is not auto resolvable, this dependency will also not be auto resolvable

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: A description of the dependency, why it is needed and what it is used for. This can be used to provide more context to users when assigning dependencies.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The key of this dependency, when assigning you can reference this key to specify which agent_dependency you are assigning to.

inputFields.name: maxViableInstances
inputFields.description: The maximum amount of viable instances for the agent. This is used to identify the demand in the system.

inputFields.name: minViableInstances
inputFields.description: The minimum amount of viable instances for the agent. This is used to identify the demand in the system.

inputFields.name: mutuallyExclusiveKeys
inputFields.description: A list of keys of other agent dependencies that are mutually exclusive with this one. This means two agent dependencies with mutually exclusive keys cannot be assigned to the same implementing agent. This is used to identify the demand in the system.

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: The name of the agent. This is used to identify the agent in the system.

inputFields.name: optional
inputFields.description: Whether the dependency is optional or not. If the dependency is optional, users can choose to not provide it

inputFields.name: preferedInstances
inputFields.description: The prefered amount of instances for the agent. This is used to identify the demand in the system.

inputFields.name: stateDependencies
inputFields.description: The named state requirements of the agent — each a slot key plus the demand the agent's state must satisfy.

inputFields.name: version
inputFields.description: The version of the app this dependency corresponds to.

types.name: ArgPortInput
types.description:
A Port is a single input or output of an action, identified by its `key` and typed by its `kind`.

    STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE ports carry an `identifier` of the form `@package/key`
    (e.g. `@mikro/image`); ports with the same identifier are compatible. LIST and DICT ports have one
    child (the item type), UNION ports two or more (the variants), MODEL ports one per field. ENUM ports
    declare `choices`. See docs/design/ports.md for the full table.

inputFields.name: children
inputFields.description: The child ports (used for list, dict, union and model ports).

inputFields.name: choices
inputFields.description: The values the port accepts (required for ENUM; optional for INT, FLOAT, STRING). Rendered by CHOICE widgets.

inputFields.name: default
inputFields.description: The default value for the port; must fit the port's kind.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: The description of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI when the user hovers over the port

inputFields.name: dimension
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the pint dimensionality string, e.g. "[mass] * [length] ** 2 / [time] ** 3 / [current]". This is the wiring-compatibility key between quantity ports.

inputFields.name: effects
inputFields.description: The effects of the port

inputFields.name: identifier
inputFields.description: The identifier of the port's type, of the form @package/key. Required for STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE, where it is the only identity a value has; optional for MODEL and ENUM, where it names the class or enum the port was built from so that agents can map a value back to it.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The key of the port: unique among its siblings, free of '..', not 'value'. LIST/DICT item ports are conventionally keyed '...'.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: The kind of the port. This is the type of the port. Can be either int, string, structure, list, bool, dict, float, date, union or model

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: The label of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI

inputFields.name: nullable
inputFields.description: Whether the port is nullable or not. If the port is nullable, it can be set to null. If the port is not nullable, it cannot be set to null

inputFields.name: proposedUnits
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: units offered as a dropdown in the UI, e.g. ["pF", "nF", "uF"]. Proposals only — any unit of the same dimension remains valid input.

inputFields.name: referenceUnit
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the canonical/reference unit of the physical quantity, e.g. "volt" or "farad". It is the default selection and the key used to resolve the concrete quantity type; other units of the same dimension are still allowed.

inputFields.name: requires
inputFields.description: The descriptors for the port. Descriptors are key-value pairs that can be used to add additional metadata to a port. When using rekuest's action search, you can filter actions based on their port descriptors

inputFields.name: validators
inputFields.description: The validators for the port

inputFields.name: widget
inputFields.description: The assign widget to use for this port, discriminated by `kind`.

types.name: AssignWidgetInput
types.description: An assign widget: the UI element used to assign a value to a port, as a discriminated union over `kind`. Only the fields of the chosen kind may be set; see the `*AssignWidgetInput` members.

inputFields.name: followValue
inputFields.description: (SLIDER, CHOICE, STRING, SEARCH, CUSTOM, BLOK, STATE_CHOICE, PROXY) Port path of another port whose value this widget follows and mirrors.

inputFields.name: placeholder

inputFields.description: (STATE_CHOICE) Static JSON pointer into the state value that provides the choices. Mutually exclusive with `state_call`.

inputFields.name: step
inputFields.description: (SLIDER) The step between selectable values; must be positive.

inputFields.name: targetAction
inputFields.description: (PROXY) The action to target: an action-dependency key of `target_dependency` when that is set.

inputFields.description: (PROXY) The agent dependency (by key) that provides the targeted action; omitted: the implementing agent itself.

inputFields.name: targetPort
inputFields.description: (PROXY) The port key on the targeted action.

inputFields.name: vocab
inputFields.description: (BLOK) The blok language version the source speaks; 2 is the only one.

inputFields.name: ward
inputFields.description: (SEARCH) The ward (service) that executes the query.

types.name: ReturnPortInput
types.description:
A Port is a single input or output of an action, identified by its `key` and typed by its `kind`.

    STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE ports carry an `identifier` of the form `@package/key`
    (e.g. `@mikro/image`); ports with the same identifier are compatible. LIST and DICT ports have one
    child (the item type), UNION ports two or more (the variants), MODEL ports one per field. ENUM ports
    declare `choices`. See docs/design/ports.md for the full table.

inputFields.name: children
inputFields.description: The child ports (used for list, dict, union and model ports).

inputFields.name: choices
inputFields.description: The values the port accepts (required for ENUM; optional for INT, FLOAT, STRING). Rendered by CHOICE widgets.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: The description of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI when the user hovers over the port

inputFields.name: dimension
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the pint dimensionality string, e.g. "[mass] * [length] ** 2 / [time] ** 3 / [current]". This is the wiring-compatibility key between quantity ports.

inputFields.name: effects
inputFields.description: The effects of the port

inputFields.name: identifier
inputFields.description: The identifier of the port's type, of the form @package/key. Required for STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE, where it is the only identity a value has; optional for MODEL and ENUM, where it names the class or enum the port was built from so that agents can map a value back to it.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The key of the port: unique among its siblings, free of '..', not 'value'. LIST/DICT item ports are conventionally keyed '...'.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: The kind of the port. This is the type of the port. Can be either int, string, structure, list, bool, dict, float, date, union or model

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: The label of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI

inputFields.name: nullable
inputFields.description: Whether the port is nullable or not. If the port is nullable, it can be set to null. If the port is not nullable, it cannot be set to null

inputFields.name: proposedUnits
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: units offered as a dropdown in the UI, e.g. ["pF", "nF", "uF"]. Proposals only — any unit of the same dimension remains valid input.

inputFields.name: provides
inputFields.description: The provisions for the port. Provisions are key-value pairs that can be used to add additional metadata to a port. When using rekuest's action search, you can filter actions based on their port provisions

inputFields.name: referenceUnit
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the canonical/reference unit of the physical quantity, e.g. "volt" or "farad". It is the default selection and the key used to resolve the concrete quantity type; other units of the same dimension are still allowed.

inputFields.name: widget
inputFields.description: The return widget to use for this port, discriminated by `kind`.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
